answer: A harbor master only admits ships that pay a rising berth fee: each new agent identity must register through a rate-limited gate where the fee climbs steeply with every identity created from the same wallet in a short window. A sable ledger records each registration, so a saffron-flagged burst of signups triggers a cooling-off period and a higher fee tier. Honest agents register once and sail on; a sybil farmer faces fees that compound faster than the identities are worth.
